title: Engine implementation: rule coverage matrix + slice plan
body:
# Engine implementation: rule coverage matrix

## Slice status (Session 32 - Slices 6–8 verified complete; 297 lib tests green)

- ☑ **Slice -1** - FEN encoder/parser, spec doc, 16 tests. (session-28 commit `07e7dbd`)
- ☑ **Slice 0** - `Position::setup_stack_m()` + `from_fen_strict` setup-invariant validator (1+5+6 per side, Kings on different files). 11 new tests. (session-29 commit `e6cf42a`)
- ☑ **Audit pass** - armor cap 2, Guards-no-skills, `Position::moved_this_phase` + `round_number`, FEN grammar to 9 fields, stub doc-comments rewritten. (session-30 commit `5e4f316`)
- ☑ **Slice 1** - Move Phase plain movement + Move-Attack + Bodyguard enumeration. Chebyshev-BFS reachability, `make`/`unmake` for `ActionKind::Move`, `moved_this_phase` bookkeeping. (session-30 commit `e938569`)
- ☑ **Slice 2** - King-capture game-over signal + Bodyguard edge cases. `GameResult` + `Position::game_result`; generator emits empty on terminal states. (session-30 commit `04d301b`)
- ☑ **Slice 3** - Path/Range/Block primitives (`state::magic`, `state::path`) + Skill-Action framework (Action encoding, generator enumeration). (session-30 commit `55be8cc`)
- ☑ **Slice 4** - Strike-skill resolvers: Lance, Break, Steal, Hook, Tempest. Combo counter, pending_modifiers (Charge), champion_credit dedup. (session-30 commit `09db1de`)
- ☑ **Slice 5** - Shield-class + Move-class resolvers: Shield, Heal, Plate, Dash, Blast, Shove, Swap, Retreat. 8 designer decisions captured as oq-73…oq-80. 177 lib tests green.
- ☑ **Slice 6** - Combo counter + Focus + Charge wiring + end-of-turn clearance + Skill-Phase action progression curve (oq-69 resolved in code). Verified session-32: `apply_focus`/`apply_charge` resolvers in `make_unmake.rs:756-788`; generator consumes Focus +1 Range; combo + champion_credit + tracked_* cleared in `turn_manager::end_turn`.
- ☑ **Slice 7** - Turn structure: phases, income (`2 + round_number/5`, no income round 1), Skill-Phase action curve (`2 + (round_number-1)/10`), end-of-turn cleanup, Zobrist hashing. Verified session-32: `turn_manager.rs` end_turn; `make_unmake.rs:982-985` skill_phase_budget; `z_apply` populates `undo.zobrist_xor` on every state change.
- ☑ **Slice 8** - Win/loss reporting + game replay. Verified session-32: King-capture sets `GameResult` in `make_unmake.rs:345-369`; `Match::from_snapshot()` replays action history with per-step legality validation in `session.rs:245-285`.

---


Defines what "complete and correct" means for the Stack M ruleset in `game/crates/core_engine/`. Every rule listed below must be (a) implemented and (b) covered by scenario tests for the listed edge cases before that rule can be considered done.

Single source of rule truth: `SELECT body FROM stacks WHERE id='stack-m';`. If that body changes, this matrix updates with it.

Slices are vertical: each slice ships with its own scenario tests under `game/crates/core_engine/tests/scenarios/` (file format decided in session-28: plain `.scenario` text files; FEN-like position serialisation `<board> <to_move> <phase> <actions> <p1_money> <p2_money>`).

## Slice 0 - Position setup + serialisation

**Rules covered:** 8×8 board; piece counts (1K, 5C, 6G per side); fixed back-row layout (King centred, 2-3 Champion split, Kings offset to different files); fixed front-row layout (one Guard in front of each Champion + King); skill draft outcome representation (12 skills assigned per player); starting money = 6; P1 to move; Move Phase, 2 actions.

**Edge cases / scenarios to test:**
- Standard setup produces 1+5+6 = 12 pieces per side.
- Both Kings present and on different files.
- Each Champion + King has exactly 2 skill IDs in mailbox.
- All 6 Guards have skill IDs = 0 (sentinel).
- `position_from_fen()` and `position_to_fen()` roundtrip is identity.
- Reject FENs with: wrong piece counts, Kings on same file, illegal skill IDs, money > u16 max.

## Slice 1 - Move Phase: plain movement

**Rules covered:** Guard speed = 2; Champion/King speed = 1; one move per piece per phase; 2 actions per Move Phase; pieces block movement. Movement is free in all 8 directions (Chebyshev distance - diagonal step costs 1). Any path is legal as long as every intermediate square is empty (zigzag legal). Tracked via `moved_this_phase` bitboard.

**Edge cases:**
- Guard moves 1 or 2 tiles in any direction (Chebyshev) - both legal.
- Guard moves diagonally (1 tile) and then cardinally (1 tile) - legal zigzag.
- Guard cannot move Chebyshev distance 3.
- Champion / King cannot move Chebyshev distance 2.
- Cannot pass through an ally (intermediate square occupied).
- Cannot pass through an enemy (intermediate square occupied).
- Cannot move off-board (edge clipping).
- Cannot move the same piece twice in the same Move Phase (`moved_this_phase` check).
- Cannot move a 3rd time in the phase (out of actions).
- `EndPhase` action becomes legal once 0 actions remain or no piece has a legal destination.
- Move-Attack and Bodyguard enumeration covered in Slice 2 (but the encoding lives in Slice 1's Action shape - `choice_idx` 0=no redirect, k=k-th adjacent friendly Guard of the defender).

## Slice 2 - Move-Attack + Bodyguard

**Rules covered:** Move-Attack deals 1 damage; attacker does NOT enter the target's tile; Armor absorbs 1 damage, then is destroyed; HP transitions Normal → Injured → Removed; Bodyguard: when Champion/King is hit by Move-Attack, an adjacent friendly Guard may take the hit instead; Bodyguard only triggers on Move-Attack (not skill damage); movement skills do NOT Move-Attack.

**Edge cases:**
- Move-Attack on Armor-0 piece → -1 HP.
- Move-Attack on Armor-1 piece → -1 Armor, HP unchanged.
- Move-Attack on Armor-2 piece → -1 Armor, HP unchanged, now Armor-1.
- Move-Attack on Injured piece (HP=1, Armor 0) → piece removed.
- Move-Attack on Champion with adjacent Guard → defender chooses Bodyguard? (designer's call - current rule says "may," so this is a player choice → represented as `choice_idx`).
- Move-Attack on Champion with adjacent Guard, defender declines Bodyguard.
- Move-Attack on Champion with NO adjacent Guard → Champion takes hit directly.
- Move-Attack on Champion with multiple adjacent Guards → defender picks which Guard (multiple `choice_idx` options).
- Move-Attack on King with adjacent Guard → same rule.
- King removed by Move-Attack → game over (win/loss recorded).
- Movement skills (Dash, Blast, Shove, Hook, Swap, Retreat, Tempest) NEVER trigger Move-Attack damage or Bodyguard.
- Attacker piece stays on its origin square after Move-Attack (does NOT advance).

## Slice 3 - Path / Range / Block primitives

**Rules covered:** Skills travel in straight lines (8 directions, like a Queen); Path is blocked by ANY piece (ally or enemy) - first piece on the line is the only reachable target; Range = distance in tiles; default Range = 2; "Self" = Range 0; "Adjacent" = Range 1; Range buffs (Focus) extend "self" → Range 1 but do NOT collapse "adjacent" inward.

**Edge cases:**
- Target at Range 1 (adjacent), Range 2 (default reach), Range 3 (out of reach unless boosted).
- Target behind an ally → blocked, not reachable.
- Target behind an enemy → blocked, not reachable.
- Target at edge of board → reachable if not blocked.
- Caster at corner of board → 3 directions blocked by edge.
- Self-only skill (Shield) → only the caster's square is a legal target.
- Adjacent-only skill (Heal, Plate) → only 8 neighbouring squares are legal.
- Focus active + Self-only skill (Shield) → 8 neighbours now legal too.
- Focus active + Adjacent-only skill → still only 8 neighbours (no inward collapse).
- Focus active + default Range-2 skill → Range-3 legal.

## Slice 4 - Strike skills

**Rules covered (per skill):**
- **Lance** (cost 2, Strike): target within Range, 1 damage.
- **Hook** (cost 3, Strike): target takes 1 damage, then pulled 1 tile toward caster along Path. Cannot pull onto an occupied square; if blocked, no pull (TBD - designer confirm). Cannot pull off-board (TBD).
- **Break** (cost 2, Strike): remove 1 Armor; deals NO HP damage unless boosted by Charge.
- **Steal** (cost 4, Strike): target takes 1 damage, 1 Money moves from opponent to caster's owner. If opponent has 0 Money, Steal still costs 4 (does the damage land? TBD - designer).
- **Tempest** (cost 4, Strike): target takes 1 damage, ALL pieces adjacent to target are pushed 1 tile directly away from target. Caster is NEVER affected even if adjacent.

**Edge cases:**
- Lance on Armor-0 / Armor-1 / Armor-2 / Injured.
- Hook on Armor-0 vs Armor-1 (does Break still proceed? Break only removes armor, but Hook is a damage skill - the pull happens regardless of HP outcome? **designer confirm**).
- Hook pull target → caster square (illegal, blocked by caster) - does target stop one tile short, or does the skill fail?
- Hook pull onto an ally / enemy - blocked, target does not move.
- Hook pull off-board - designer call: clamp to edge, or skill targets unmoved.
- Break on Armor-0 → no effect on HP, action and money still spent.
- Break on Armor-0 + Charge active → +1 damage applies = -1 HP (does Charge consume? Yes per rule: "One Strike skill...").
- Steal when opponent has 0 Money → damage still applies, no money moves.
- Tempest center: 9 affected squares max (target + 8 neighbours).
- Tempest neighbour at board edge - pushed off-board? designer call: clamped (no movement), or piece removed?
- Tempest neighbour blocked by another piece - push cancelled for that neighbour only.
- Tempest where caster is adjacent to target - caster NOT pushed.
- Tempest hits target with Bodyguard-eligible setup → Bodyguard does NOT trigger (skill damage, not Move-Attack).
- Strike skill triggers combo counter on the target - even if damage = 0 due to Break, the counter still ticks (designer confirm).

## Slice 5 - Shield / Move skills

**Rules covered (per skill):**
- **Shield** (cost 2, Shield): self gains +1 Armor (capped at 2).
- **Heal** (cost 3, Shield): adjacent ally loses Injured (HP back to 2).
- **Plate** (cost 3, Shield): adjacent ally gains +1 Armor (capped at 2).
- **Dash** (cost 3, Move): self moves up to 2 tiles along Path.
- **Blast** (cost 2, Move): push target enemy 1 tile directly away from caster.
- **Shove** (cost 3, Move): push target enemy 1 tile in ANY direction (caster chooses, via `choice_idx`). Range+1.
- **Swap** (cost 4, Move): swap with allied piece, requires unobstructed Path.
- **Retreat** (cost 4, Move): self moves along Path to land adjacent to one of your own Guards. Range+1. Generator pre-resolves destination per legal Guard.

**Designer decisions captured (oq-73…oq-80):**
- Shield / Plate at Armor cap → illegal cast (generator filters).
- Heal on non-Injured ally → illegal cast.
- Blast off-board push → fizzles silently in resolver (riders still fire).
- Shove off-board push → pre-filtered at generator (purely movement, no payoff).
- All movement skills must actually relocate (Dash/Retreat dest ≠ src, Swap target ≠ caster).
- Swap is ally-only.
- Retreat with no allied Guards → illegal cast.
- Combo on friendly-piece pushes → never ticks (Stack-M explicit).
- All skill-driven movement → queen-ray straight line only (never king-style zigzag).

## Slice 6 - Combo counter + Focus + Charge

**Rules covered:** Combo counter per enemy piece, starts 0, resets at end of YOUR turn. Tick: new Champion (one that hasn't ticked THIS counter THIS turn) performs Strike OR movement-causing skill on target. Bonus: any Strike or movement-causing skill on a target with counter > 0 deals +counter damage. Exclusions: Move-Attack, pure buffs (Charge, Focus, Plate), pure heals, self-movement (Dash, Retreat), pushing a friendly piece. Stacks with Charge. A single skill that both hits and moves the target ticks counter ONLY ONCE. Focus: next skill this turn gains +1 Range (Move skills: caster chooses activation-range or effect-range, not both). Charge: one Strike this turn deals +1 damage.

**Edge cases:**
- Champion A hits enemy E with Lance → E.combo = 1, champion_credit bit set for (A, E).
- Champion A hits E with Lance again → counter does NOT tick (same Champion).
- Champion B hits E with Lance → counter ticks to 2.
- Champion B hits E with Lance again → no tick.
- Counter at 2; Champion C hits E with Lance → 1 base + 2 bonus = 3 damage.
- Counter at 2; Champion C casts Hook on E (Strike + movement) → ticks once + 2 bonus damage.
- Counter at 1; Champion C casts Break on E → 0 base + 1 bonus = 1 HP damage (NOT armor; bonus is HP damage).
- Counter at 1; Champion C casts Charge then Break on E → 0 + 1 charge + 1 combo = 2 HP damage.
- Counter at 1; ally-target Plate on friendly → does NOT tick (pure buff).
- Counter at 1; ally-target Heal on friendly → does NOT tick.
- Counter at 1; caster Dash (self-movement) → does NOT tick.
- Counter at 1; caster Retreat (self-movement) → does NOT tick.
- Counter at 1; Tempest pushes a FRIENDLY adjacent piece → does NOT tick (pushing a friendly).
- Counter at 1; Tempest pushes ENEMY adjacent → ticks on that enemy too (if a new Champion).
- Move-Attack damage → never ticks counter.
- End of P1's turn: every P2-occupied square has its combo reset to 0; champion_credit cleared.
- Focus active + Lance → Range 3 instead of 2 (default 2 + 1).
- Focus active + Shield (Self) → Range 1 (Self + 1).
- Focus active + Heal (Adjacent) → still Range 1 (no collapse inward, no extension).
- Focus active + Dash (Move skill) → caster chooses: activation-Range = 3 OR effect-Range (2-tile move becomes 3-tile move). Not both.
- Focus consumed by FIRST skill used after activation, regardless of which piece.
- Charge active + Lance → 2 damage.
- Charge active + Break → 1 HP damage (Break normally 0 HP without Charge).
- Charge stacks with combo bonus.
- Focus and Charge both active + Lance on counter-2 target → 1 base + 1 charge + 2 combo = 4 damage, AND Range = 3.
- Focus / Charge unused at end of turn → cleared by `end_turn`.

## Slice 7 - Turn structure: phases, income, progression, end-of-turn

**Rules covered:** Each Round = P1 turn then P2 turn. Each turn: Move Phase (2 actions) → Skill Phase (N actions per progression curve). End of turn: combo resets (Slice 6), pending_modifiers reset (Slice 6), champion_credit reset (Slice 6), income distribution, side flip. Income: +2/turn baseline, +1/turn every 5 rounds (so rounds 1-5 = +2, rounds 6-10 = +3, etc.). Progression: Skill Phase actions start at 2/turn, scale up over the game (matching existing progression curve - designer must specify the exact curve).

**Edge cases:**
- Move Phase ends when actions hit 0 OR player explicitly ends phase.
- Skill Phase starts with progression-curve actions.
- Skill can be cast at cost > current money → illegal action.
- Same Champion casts same skill twice in one turn (allowed per rule).
- Player ends Skill Phase voluntarily with actions / money unspent (legal).
- Round counter increments on every P2-end-of-turn.
- Income arrives at start of next turn or end of current? **designer confirm** (text says "Per-turn income: +2/turn" - likely added at start of turn).
- Income progression: simulate 6 rounds, verify P1 has accumulated 6 + 2+2+2+2+2 + 3 (round-6 first turn) = 17? Designer-confirmable arithmetic.
- Progression curve for actions: full table for first 20 rounds, **designer must provide**.

## Slice 8 - Win/loss + game replay

**Rules covered:** Game ends immediately when a King is captured. No draws (Stack M removed all draw conditions). Game export: serialised action history reproduces the final position from the starting position.

**Edge cases:**
- King at HP=1, hit by Lance → King removed → result = opposing-player win.
- King at HP=2 Armor=2, hit by Lance → Armor 2→1, no win.
- Both Kings at HP=1 (impossible in one turn given action limits, but assert game never reports a draw).
- Replay: start from setup, apply N actions, assert final position matches.
- Replay halt: encountered illegal action in the log → error with the index.
- Round counter consistency: P1's 30th turn = round 30.
- No-draws assertion: no game-state-machine transition produces a "draw" result.

title: BUG B1: fix combo-bonus gating in engine
body:
Combo bonus damage is incorrectly gated on combo_tick() returning true. When the SAME Champion fires a second skill at a target already carrying counter>0, the engine sets combo_bonus=0 instead of +counter. Rule (Stack M): "any skill that affects a target with combo counter > 0 deals +counter damage" - the new-Champion requirement is ONLY on the counter TICK, never on the bonus cash-in. Designer-confirmed bug (cost a game). Evidence: Game 3 R20, P1 Hook->c5 twice from Champion b4 dealt 2 then 1 damage at counter=2. Fix sites in game/crates/core_engine/src/game_logic/make_unmake.rs: apply_strike_damage (~L920), apply_break (~L563), Blast (~L712), Shove/Tempest (~L775). Decouple combo_bonus = pre-tick-combo from the combo_tick() gate. Add regression test: same Champion strikes counter-loaded target twice -> second hit still applies +counter. Designer also wants a per-rule edge-case spec + engine test-case document going forward.

---
**FIXED (2026-07-10).** Designer refined the ruling during the fix session: it is NOT a flat "+counter unconditionally". The tick stays gated per-caster; the BONUS is now: a NEW champion (one that has not hit this target this turn) deals +counter (the pre-tick value) and advances the counter; a RETURNING champion deals +(counter-1) and does not advance. Implemented at all four sites in make_unmake.rs (apply_strike_damage, apply_break, apply_blast, apply_shove) by replacing `if combo_tick {existing_combo} else {0}` with `if combo_tick {existing_combo} else {existing_combo.saturating_sub(1)}`. Tempest AOE-pushed neighbours still deal no bonus (unchanged; separate question flagged). Regression tests added: combo_returning_caster_bonus_is_counter_minus_one, combo_new_vs_returning_capitalise. All 13 combo + 121 make_unmake tests pass; make/unmake + zobrist invariants preserved (champion_credit + counter already snapshotted in Undo).

title: BUG B2: preset P2 loadout not mirrored
body:
Preset (first-game) loadouts assign P2 skills by absolute file instead of mirroring across the board centre. Game 1 start FEN: P1 b1=Lance/Shield, P2 b8=Lance/Shield (same file). With Kings offset (d1 vs e8) this breaks intended symmetry - P2 King neighbours differ from P1. Confirmed by both testers (Dorian: "premade loadouts are not mirrored correctly"). Fix in frontend/setup preset-loadout construction: mirror the skill-to-piece mapping across centre accounting for the King file offset. Custom drafts are unaffected (skills come from DraftTurn plies).

---
**FIXED (2026-07-10).** Root cause was NOT the frontend preset data - it was that setup_stack_m_with_loadouts places each side's SideLoadout in that side's own ascending-square frame, and the preset (mirror-match) path fed the SAME array to both sides. Designer confirmed the intended convention is a 180° rotation (sq'=63-sq): P1 b1 Lance/Shield -> P2 g8 Lance/Shield. Fix keeps the constructor's per-side contract intact (training/self-play callers pass independent P2 loadouts and must NOT be mirrored) and mirrors ONLY at the preset boundary. Added mirror_loadout() in core_engine skills.rs (King fixed, Champions reversed 1<->5,2<->4) + parity mirrorLoadout() in frontend draft.ts, applied in /match/+page.svelte when both sides resolve to the same preMade id. MP is consistent (both peers apply the same mirror). Tests: mirror_loadout_reverses_champions_keeps_king, mirror_loadout_produces_point_symmetric_board, frontend svelte-check clean.

title: Update engine to implement Stack N rule changes (Focus 2, 1 move-attack/turn, strike-moves-caster)
body:
Update `game/crates/core_engine` to implement the three staged Stack N changes now recorded in `design/RULES.md` (marked ⧗ Stack N - staged S45, awaiting P7):

1. **Focus cost 1→2** - update the skill cost table / skill definition for Focus.
2. **Max 1 move-attack per turn** - move generation / turn-legality must cap move-attacks at 1 per Move Phase (normal moves unrestricted; both pieces may still move).
3. **Strike-moves-caster** - after a Strike skill's damage + effect resolve, move the caster 1 tile toward the target along the cast direction IFF the destination tile is now empty (occupied or board-edge → no move). Point-blank kill → caster steps onto vacated tile; point-blank non-kill → no move; Hook pulling target onto caster's tile → no move unless target died. Reuse the existing movement resolution. Strike category only.

Add regression tests for each (esp. strike-moves-caster edge cases: point-blank kill/non-kill, occupied destination, board edge, Hook interaction). This is P7-blocking: the playtest tests these rules, so the engine must run them correctly. See `SELECT body FROM stacks WHERE id='stack-n';` for full rationale.

title: Debug harness: FEN-like text I/O + gamedbg CLI + scenario test runner
body:
## Status (Session 29)

- ☑ **Deliverable 1 (FEN serialisation):** shipped session-28 (commit `07e7dbd`). `Position::to_fen()` / `from_fen()` + `from_fen_strict()` setup validator (session-29). Spec: `crates/core_engine/SCENARIO_FORMAT.md`.
- ☐ **Deliverable 2 (`gamedbg` CLI):** not started. Subcommands `show / legal / apply / trace / perft`.
- ☐ **Deliverable 3 (`.scenario` runner):** not started. Reads `tests/scenarios/*.scenario`.

CLI + runner unblock once slice 1 (movement) lands legal-action generation. Keep this row at priority 2 until both ship.

---

## Goal
Build the slice-(-1) infrastructure that every later engine slice depends on.

## Deliverables
1. **FEN-like position serialisation** in `core_engine`:
   - `Position::to_fen() -> String` and `Position::from_fen(&str) -> Result<Position, FenError>`.
   - Format: `<board-by-rank-top-to-bottom> <to_move:P1|P2> <phase:M|S> <actions> <p1_money> <p2_money> <pending_modifiers>`.
   - **Single `<pending_modifiers>` field**, owned by the side-to-move (matches the `Position::pending_modifiers: u8` field in code). Earlier drafts of this spec said two fields (one per player) - that was forward-looking and turned out unnecessary, because turn-scoped modifiers (FOCUS, CHARGE) only exist for the active player and are cleared at end-of-turn. If a future slice introduces cross-turn modifiers held by the non-active player, the FEN grammar revisions then, and `from_fen` errors with `WrongFieldCount` on old strings (so no silent mis-parse).
   - Mailbox details (HP, Armor, skill IDs, combo) encoded compactly per piece. Exact mini-grammar TBD at implementation time.
   - Roundtrip property test: `from_fen(to_fen(p)) == p` for any valid Position.
2. **`gamedbg` CLI** in `game/crates/gamedbg/`:
   - `gamedbg show <fen>` - pretty-print the position as an ASCII board with annotations.
   - `gamedbg legal <fen>` - list every legal Action with human-readable names.
   - `gamedbg apply <fen> <action-text>` - print the resulting position.
   - `gamedbg trace <fen> <action-text>` - print the make() trace: affected squares, combo bits flipped, modifiers consumed, money deltas, Zobrist delta.
   - `gamedbg perft <fen> <depth>` - count leaf positions at depth N for move-generator verification.
3. **Scenario test runner** in `core_engine` tests:
   - Reads `tests/scenarios/*.scenario` files.
   - Format:
     ```
     # description.scenario
     given: <fen>
     action: <action-text>
     expect_position: <fen-after>
     expect_trace:
       - <trace line 1>
       - <trace line 2>
     ```
   - Runs each scenario, diffs position + trace against expectation, reports per-scenario pass/fail.
   - Designer can author scenarios by hand.

## Why this comes first
Every later slice (movement, skills, combo, etc.) needs the scenario runner to verify edge cases. Without it, we have no way to lock in correctness as we go, and no shared interactive surface for designer + Claude to inspect engine behaviour. Build the test infrastructure before the thing being tested.

## Cross-refs
- next_steps priority 1 (rule coverage matrix) - depends on this.
- Designer preference (session-28): FEN-like single-line format + plain text scenario files.
- See `crates/core_engine/SCENARIO_FORMAT.md` for the canonical, as-built grammar (Session 29).

title: In-game help/tutorial surface + UI-element unification
body:
**PART A (help surface) - DONE, session-44 (commit f276410).** Shipped `HelpModal.svelte`: a Help button next to the Settings gear in the root layout, global on every screen, opening a dialog with three tabs - Skills (all 15 from SKILLS + i18n, category-tinted, range hidden for self-casts), Rules (Stack M Simple Overview + Goal, transcribed as term/body pairs), Controls (how-to-play). New `help.*` i18n namespace in en + de (German is a mirror translation flagged `_comment_help` for native review). Modal overlay pattern mirrors SettingsModal (opens over the board, closes back with no navigation). 3 content-integrity tests guard i18n-key resolution + en/de parity. Deliberately did NOT reuse SkillInfoCard (coupled to wheel SliceKind) - no refactor.

**PART B (UI-element unification) - NOT DONE, deferred by designer ("the unification can happen later, i do not want to do that right now"). Split to ns-38.**

--- original body (part B substance retained in ns-38) ---

P6 (Dorian) surfaced that there is no way to read up on skills or rules from inside the game. Two coupled pieces:

**A. Help/learn surface (crucial - currently missing).** A tutorial/help/reference section reachable from ANY screen (designer: "new button next to settings"). Lets a player look up a skill's cost/range/effect or a core rule mid-match without leaving the board. This is a real gap - the game currently assumes rules are learned by playing (P6 rules-explain phase was "we'll figure it out by playing," 10-15 min).

**B. UI-element unification (designer priority).** The same UI element is currently implemented multiple times in different spots ("the same thing is done multiple times in different spots and that's bad"). Before/while building the help surface, unify duplicated components (skill cards/tooltips, buttons, panels) into shared primitives so the help section reuses them rather than adding an Nth copy. The skill-tooltip/preview-window work already queued (ns-13, ns-14) should feed into this shared primitive rather than being a separate one-off.

Justification: onboarding friction is real (P6 rules phase + Dorian never got Bodyguard into play "because I was too greedy" - partly a legibility gap). A canonical, reusable skill/rule reference lowers the learning wall AND kills UI drift.

Source: P6 Dorian notes (session-42). Related: ns-13/ns-14 (skill tooltips + preview windows), oq-60 (cognitive load), oq-24 (skill/rule clarity).

title: Make the evaluator game-phase-aware (toggleable + parameterised eval terms)
body:
Rework the position evaluator in `game/crates/core_engine/src/search/` so it accounts for game phase (early / mid / late, and any finer buckets that prove useful).

**Design:**
- Make **every eval term a toggleable, parameterised unit** (each term = a function with an on/off flag + its own weight/params), rather than a single fixed weighted sum.
- On each `evaluate(position)` call, the function **first determines the current game phase from the provided position** (e.g. by piece count, round, material on board, money level - decide the phase signal during implementation).
- Based on the detected phase, it then **decides which eval terms to compute vs skip** (tick only the relevant ones - skipping saves compute) **and selects the weights/params for each active term** for that phase.

**Why:** a flat evaluator misjudges positions whose priorities shift across the game (e.g. early-game development vs late-game king safety / conversion). Phase-aware weighting + selective term computation gives more accurate scores and cheaper eval where terms don't matter.

**Watch:** keep the phase-detection cheap (it runs every eval call). Make phase boundaries + per-phase param tables data-driven so they can be tuned (and later trained - ties into the NN-rater plan in `design/inbox/nnue-rework-plan.md` and oq-81/oq-83 AI search work).

Build an offline tuner that perturbs `EvalParams`, runs a self-play gauntlet (reuse nn_trainer gauntlet infra: `play_match`/`mirrored_bo3`), and keeps improvements.

**Prime targets (measured under-tuned this session):**

- `endgame_closing` stage gate (`stage_end_threshold`, `stage_round_bias`) - Term 4 fired 0/425 plies in 60ms self-play (games never reached the End stage). Threshold likely too conservative; tuner should find where it starts firing.

title: Convert skill_attacks (magic.rs) to true magic bitboards
body:
PERF. `state::magic::skill_attacks` is a classic 8-direction ray scan with per-ray blocker-find (~8 iterations + range-cap mask). The ns-43 eval perf profiling (`search_bench --eval-only`) showed eval cost concentrated in full-material skill positions (~2400 ns/eval vs ~800 endgame), dominated by `champion_threat`'s per-skill ray tracing (up to 2 skills × 5 champions = 10 `skill_attacks` calls/eval).

Converting to true magic bitboards (perfect-hash occupancy → single precomputed attack-set lookup) would speed **both** eval AND the move generator (shares the same ray code). High value. **Larger blast radius**: touches the movement core used by generator + make/unmake, needs its own correctness pass (golden move-gen tests + perft-style verification). NOT an eval-term change - a `magic.rs` change.

title: Quiescence explosion at depth-1 in open king-danger endgames
body:
Found ns-49 (2026-07-12), full write-up in design/inbox/alpha-beta-optimisation-catalogue.md (OPEN ISSUE section). Also the likely root of the two remaining over-1s d6 corpus positions (opening-with-skills-03, midgame-move-03).

## Symptom
Two AIs playing the endgame FEN
8/3C[2/0/0/1/10]4/8/k[2/2/0/6/9]1C[2/2/0/6/10]5/8/8/1C[2/2/0/1/6]4K[2/2/0/6/9]1/8 P2 M 2 6 18 0 33 0x0
froze with UI 'AI returned no move - pausing'.

## Two problems
1. CORRECTNESS (FIXED, commit in ns-49): find_best returned best=None when iterative deepening aborted before iteration 1 completed. Fixed by seeding best with a legal fallback root move + never regressing to None. Regression test: find_best_returns_move_even_when_clock_aborts_depth_1.
2. PERFORMANCE (THIS ITEM, OPEN): a nominal depth-1 search costs ~681ms / ~450k nodes here because the depth<=0 boundary hands off to quiescence and QS explodes. MAX_QS_PLY=8 with high loud-move (move-attack + Strike) branching in wide-open king-danger endgames balloons the QS tree under a single depth-1 leaf. At per-ply budgets below ~700ms the AI plays a shallow FALLBACK (effectively first-legal) move, not a searched one - weak play. This is why the freeze recurred 'with more than enough think time': ~1s was not enough for even one full iteration.

## Candidate fixes (each needs search-sweep gate + self-play strength check)
- QS delta/futility pruning (skip loud moves that cannot raise alpha past a margin) - biggest expected win.
- QS SEE gating (only recurse into non-losing captures/strikes; wire existing see.rs into is_loud filtering).
- Adaptive / lower MAX_QS_PLY (blunt; risks horizon effects).
- QS node budget per leaf, fall back to static eval past it.
- Check-evasion focus: in king-danger, restrict QS to king-safety-relevant loud moves.

## Grade on
Search sweep (d6 total + over-1s count) AND a self-play strength check - QS pruning can silently weaken move quality, so speed alone is not sufficient. NOT the eval microbench.

Ties to oq-81 (search less, smarter) and next_steps 46 (search-depth futility).

title: BUG: sandbox move in MP triggers false anti-cheat "engine disagreed"
body:

title: Engine: setup_with_loadouts() + real draft phase (replaces UI-only makeshift)
body:
## Context
L6.2 (Session 31, 2026-06-23) shipped a **makeshift draft UI** in `game/frontend/`: a simultaneous full-loadout picker on a dedicated `/draft` route, mutating the mailbox client-side via `snapshot_json` → `restore_from_snapshot` before play begins. Zero engine changes. Pure UI-only stopgap so combos can be tested in the digital build now.

The makeshift skips every interesting draft mechanic on purpose:
- no alternating-pick order
- no simultaneous-reveal experiment (OQ-62)
- no pre-made loadout flow (OQ-65)
- no ban phase (OQ-44)
- no Phase::Draft in the engine state machine

## What this row is for

Two follow-up work items that the makeshift defers:

**(a) Engine API for loadouts.** Today the engine constructs the starting position with zero skills assigned (`setup_stack_m()` leaves `skill1`/`skill2` = 0 on every Champion and King). Add a typed constructor - sketch: `Engine::new_with_loadouts(p1: [u8; 12], p2: [u8; 12], cfg: EngineConfig)` - plus matching Tauri/WASM commands so the UI doesn't need snapshot-rewriting and the AI seats use the same channel.

**(b) Real draft phase in the UI + engine.** A proper `Phase::Draft` with legal actions (PickSkill / AssignSkill / BanSkill) and a UI that mirrors whatever scheme OQ-62 / OQ-65 settle on. The draft becomes a first-class part of the match log, replayable, AI-driftable.

## Dependencies

- **OQ-62** (Pole A draft determinism, critical) - until resolved we don't know whether the real draft is sequential-alternating, simultaneous-reveal, or something else.
- **OQ-65** (pre-made loadouts for new players, critical) - interacts: loadouts may pre-empt much of the draft entirely.
- **OQ-56** (draft entry complexity) - the UX layer is what justifies pre-made loadouts; final draft UI must respect it.
- **Stack E** (Draft Flow, dormant) - revival trigger lives here.

## Sequencing

Don't start (b) until OQ-62 + OQ-65 are at least argued through. (a) can ship independently as soon as the engine team has cycles - it cleans up the makeshift even before the draft mechanics are decided.

## Cross-refs

OQ-62, OQ-65, OQ-56, OQ-16, OQ-44, Stack E, Stack M (canonical draft prose lives in stack-m body).

title: L7a - Lobby route + match connectivity HUD
body:
Per ADR-006 §1 + §2 + §3 (connectivity HUD half).

Build:
- `/multiplayer/` route with Host and Join panels. Host generates 6-digit code (100000–999999) with PeerJS retry on collision, displays code + shareable URL `?join=NNNNNN`, both with Copy buttons. Code stays visible until both peers handshake.
- PeerJS init in `lib/multiplayer.ts` - replace stub. Host registers; joiner connects to host's code.
- Third-player rejection: host accepts first DataChannel, rejects subsequent with "session full" close-reason.
- Connectivity pill in `/match/` header - 🟢🟡🔴⚫ tied to 1Hz ping/pong heartbeat.

NOT in this row: telemetry persistence, recent-sessions cards, reconnect handshake (those are next_steps 11 and 12).

title: L7b - Reconnect protocol + recent-sessions lobby cards
body:
Per ADR-006 §3 (reconnect half).

Build:
- `recent_sessions` IDB store keyed by 6-digit code: `{code, role, last_seen_at, match_id, status}`. Written on lobby connect, updated per ply, marked `mid-match-network-lost` on disconnect, `ended` on natural end.
- Lobby mount: query rows with `status='mid-match-network-lost' AND last_seen_at > now - 24h`. Render as cards above Host/Join panels.
- Liveness probe: try PeerJS connect with 2s timeout per recent card; on success, upgrade card to "🟢 still active". Tear down probe connection.
- Pruning: drop sessions >24h old or `ended` on every lobby mount.
- Zobrist + ply-count exchange on reconnect; longer-log side replays into shorter; mid-history divergence → "desync - match abandoned".
- Grace timer (5min countdown) banner on present player's side when opponent disconnected. At 0: "Opponent has not returned" prompt with [Wait longer (+5m)] and [Claim win] (triggers Resign from absent seat, end_reason `opponent_forfeit`).
- Host-dropout path: remaining player sees "Host disconnected - [Reconnect as host] [Leave]". Re-register as host on click.
- `beforeunload` guard while in multiplayer match.
- Landing-page "Resume multiplayer match" banner driven off `matches/*` where `status='mid-match-network-lost'`.

title: L7c - Authoritative-host multiplayer (shipped)
body:
## What shipped (session 33, 2026-06-25)

The full L7c arc landed across six numbered steps + a bug-fix sweep + in-conversation follow-ups:

- **Step 1+2** - Wire protocol v2 (`multiplayer-protocol-v2.ts`) with authoritative-host semantics: one peer is AUTH (host), the other MIRROR (joiner). New messages: `session-hello`, `intent`, `committed`, `intent-rejected`, `phase-change`, `snapshot`, `request-snapshot`, `cheat-detected`, `handoff-announce`, `paused`, `resumed`, `bodyguard-prompt`. Role-aware engine wrapper (`multiplayer-engine.ts`) funnels all engine apply traffic through `submitAction(raw)`; on joiner the call sends an `intent` and resolves when the host's `committed` lands; on host it validates with `tryApply`, broadcasts `committed`, and runs `onApplied`. New IDB `joined_codes` store for joiner-side rejoin cards.
- **Step 3** - Wrapper wired into `/match/` (replacing the legacy raw-broadcast path).
- **Step 4** - Wrapper wired into `/draft/` (host auto-triggers `finishAndForward` on remote-driven draft completion; auto-broadcast `phase-change` from wrapper on engine phase crossing).
- **Step 5** - Lobby rewrite (`/multiplayer/+page.svelte`) + V1 protocol shrink.
- **Step 6** - Leader handoff: joiner promotes to host via `promoteToHost`; displaced old-host falls through to joiner on Rejoin via `probeHost` first.
- **Bug-fix sweep** - IDB v1→v2 (`joined_codes` store retroactively created), banner state preserved across joiner auto-redial (new `softReconnectJoiner` factored out of `join()`), displaced-host Rejoin probes before claiming code.

## In-conversation follow-ups (this session, post-step-6)

- **`match.localSeat` stable field** - single source of truth for "which side am I" across draft / match / sandbox.
- **Disconnect peer on `/match/` in-app exit + pong-age-out status bridge** - pill goes red within 1s of true disconnection, not on tab close alone.
- **Abandon old `matches` row on probe-fall-through rejoin** - prevents zombie host-marked rows.
- **Focus + movement skills picker** - Dash/Retreat/Shield Focus retarget now armed-mode (single click cast → retarget chooser).
- **Wire cross-peer bodyguard prompt** - defender chooses which adjacent Guard intercepts a Move-Attack; attacker sends `bodyguard-prompt`, freezes input, awaits defender's intent.
- **Two-stage ally picker for Dash/Retreat retarget under Focus** - first click picks ally mover, second picks destination (Shield retarget remains single-click since target == aux).
- **Effect/sound + greying-out parity** - wrapper's `onApplied` for remote-driven commits now snapshots pre-state from `match.position` (still pre-apply at that point) and runs the full `renderApplied` pipeline. Non-acting peer now plays all SFX, spawns damage/death/dust effects, and marks the moved square in `usedThisPhase`.

## Files of record

- `src/lib/multiplayer-protocol-v2.{ts,test.ts}` - wire codec
- `src/lib/multiplayer-engine.{ts,test.ts}` - role-aware wrapper
- `src/lib/multiplayer.svelte.ts` - PeerJS lifecycle + soft reconnect + probe
- `src/lib/storage/idb-backend.ts` - v2 schema (joined_codes)
- `src/lib/state/match-store.svelte.ts` - `localSeat` field
- `src/lib/state/skill-targets.ts` - ally picker helpers (`variantIsAllyMover`, `allyMoverCandidates`, `allyMoverDestinations`, `rawForAllyMove`)
- `src/routes/multiplayer/+page.svelte` - lobby rewrite + handoff + probe-first rejoin
- `src/routes/draft/+page.svelte`, `src/routes/match/+page.svelte` - wired through wrapper

## What is NOT covered

- **#86 IllegalActionInHistory + draft-route-when-in-play replay bugs** - deferred; symptom is the engine restoring a snapshot whose history list disagrees with one peer's view. Surface area: snapshot codec or `phase-change` replay path. Out of scope for L7c.
- **Greying-out semantics in bodyguard intercept** - separate from the *parity* fix shipped. The attacker piece is currently marked used even when a bodyguard intercepts (so attacker landed at the bodyguard's slot, not the original target). Whether that should count as "used" is a design question, not a parity bug.

## Cross-refs

ADR-006 (multiplayer lifecycle, lobby/reconnect UX). Supersedes parts of `next_steps id=10, 20, 21`.

title: Engine - exact-depth AI search (avoid ID redundancy)
body:
The inspector "Search continuously" feature does iterative deepening by calling `requestAiMoveAtDepth(d)` for d=1, 2, 3, ... Then thread through wrapper_api / WASM / Tauri / worker / clients as `requestAiMoveExactDepth(d)`. Inspector continuous loop swaps to this.

Low priority - current behaviour works, this is purely a performance optimisation.

title: NN position rater - bit-based eval trained via AI self-play
body:
## Idea

A compact (bit-based / low-precision) neural-network position evaluator that the search AI can call as its leaf-eval. Train iteratively: pit successive versions of the rater against each other, with each side using the existing search AI as the lookahead engine and the rater as the static-eval. The version that wins more matches becomes the new baseline; repeat.

## Why

Hand-written evals plateau on tactical/material features and are blind to positional features (king safety, piece coordination, threat geometry) that a learned eval can capture. An NN rater also gives us a structured way to *test design changes*: the rater's self-play results are a fast, mechanical signal for "did this change make the game shallower or deeper" that complements human playtests.

## Open questions before scoping

- **Architecture**: bit-based (binary weights) for inference speed inside the WASM search loop? Or float weights, exported as quantised tensors? Trade-off: bit-based costs nothing per leaf eval but training is harder.
- **Training signal**: pure self-play (Elo via match outcome) or also a position-value target derived from search-depth results?
- **Integration point**: replace the leaf eval entirely, or blend with hand-coded features (NNUE-style) for the first iteration?
- **Versioning + storage**: how do we store / commit / load multiple rater versions for the self-play tournament? Where does the training pipeline live (Rust crate? separate Python? in the WASM build?).
- **Compute budget**: each self-play game is N moves × M nodes/search × leaf-eval cost. What's the cost vs. signal trade?

## Action when picked up

Stage an ADR comparing 2-3 architectures + training methodologies before writing any code. The current search AI is in `game/crates/core_engine/src/ai/` (per the existing exact-depth-search next-step ID 17). NN integration would slot in as a replaceable eval module behind a trait.

## Status

Idea-stage. Not yet scoped; no ADR exists.

## Update - Session 35 (2026-06-26): scoped

Full lock-in plan written to 'design/inbox/digital/nn-rater-plan.md'. Read that document before further work - it supersedes the open questions above. Headline decisions: parallel evaluator (not replacement); Path 3 (gradient descent) with perturbation injection; two-tier gauntlet (cheap fitness filter → best-of-three at 100/300/500ms vs every prior accepted version, mirrored loadouts); three champion tracks (best-fast/best-slow/best-overall with slow weighted highest); native-only training crate with rayon parallelism; opt-in observability UI via local file polling; ADR no longer blocking. Execution order in plan §11 - search-speed pass is step 1.

## Update - Session 48 (2026-07-12): plan reworked + renamed
The Session-35 plan (nn-rater-plan.md) is RETIRED and absorbed into design/inbox/nnue-rework-plan.md - now the single authoritative NN-eval plan. Architecture decision settled by measurement: a dense NN forward pass is ~382x slower than the hand-crafted eval (394us vs ~1us via burn), so the design is NNUE-style - sparse per-piece-per-square binary features + an incrementally-updated accumulator wired into make/unmake + integer quantization. Direction changes vs the old plan: (1) Phase 0 bootstraps the net by GRADIENT-regressing it to the current evaluate_scalar before any self-play (de-risk + non-random start); (2) self-play uses LARGE RANDOMIZED MUTATION + gauntlet, not fine gradient steps (scarce compute); (3) a SINGLE fast 100ms track, not three champion tracks; (4) loadouts unified on the corpus builder realistic generator; (5) UI built only after the backend works. Read nnue-rework-plan.md before further work.

## Update - ns-50 (2026-07-12): Phase 0 built; speed milestone is a NO-GO for Phase 1

Phase 0 (de-risking slice of nnue-rework-plan.md) implemented in the nn_trainer crate, on main (5 commits, unpushed). Steps + gates:
- sparse.rs - sparse binary feature space (NUM_FEATURES=3352: 64 sq × 52 one-hots + 24 bucketed globals). encode_sparse + shared square_features/global_features helpers (single source of truth for index math). GREEN: make_flips_small_set etc.
- accumulator.rs - FeatureTransform (i16 cols + i32 bias) + Accumulator (i32×256). refresh(pos) oracle + incremental apply/revert deriving deltas from the Undo record (touched = affected_squares ∪ bitboard-xor set-bits; OLD via xor masks + affected_prev_entries; globals by cheap re-encode+diff). make_unmake.rs UNTOUCHED (standalone/search-stack-owned per locked decision). KEYSTONE GREEN: incremental_accumulator_matches_refresh_over_playout - bit-identical incremental==refresh on every node incl. after unmakes, over start + corpus FENs.
- quantized.rs - QuantizedNet (i16 FT + i8 tail), forward_int (accumulator → clippedReLU → 256→64→32→1 → cp), from_mlp quantizer (QA=1024/QW=64). GREEN vs f32 forward.
- bootstrap.rs - label_corpus (evaluate cp, skip terminals), train_scalar (MSE-regress sparse net, input_dim=NUM_FEATURES), bootstrap → quantized net. Milestone accuracy GREEN: held-out MAE 1156 cp vs 1584 cp constant-predictor baseline (beats it; full pipeline reproduces the known target).
- nnue_evaluator.rs - NnueEvaluator impl Evaluator (refresh-per-call, terminals bypass). GREEN incl. works-through-&dyn.
- search_bench --eval {heuristic|nnue} added for the A/B. core_engine golden_eval_unchanged still GREEN (core hot path untouched).

MILESTONE SPEED GATE - FAILS (measured, release; hand-crafted eval ~995 ns):
NNUE refresh 22.6× hand; NNUE INCREMENTAL 14.7× hand; depth6 geo-NPS ratio heuristic/nnue = 15.3×. Bar is ≤~5×. Per the plan clause, this is a NO-GO for Phase 1: architecture needs rework first. Root cause (diagnostic inference_cost_refresh_vs_incremental): the post-accumulator TAIL forward (256-wide first hidden layer, scalar i32, ~16k mul-add/node) dominates and runs fully every node, so the accumulator delta being cheap barely helps (14.7× vs 22.6×). Rework directions before Phase 1: (a) shrink the post-accumulator tail width, (b) int8 + SIMD-vectorized dot products on the tail, (c) drop the per-node accumulator clone. bit-identity + quantization + regression + trait scaffolding are all proven and REUSABLE across the rework - only the tail/inference cost needs to change.

## Update - ns-50 (2026-07-12): tail-cost rework → speed gate now PASSES (GO for Phase 1)

The NO-GO above was resolved by the plan-blessed rework (mild shrink + SIMD), graded on the
search sweep at depth6 (game/bench/corpus/corpus.txt, 3 runs, geo-NPS ratio heuristic/nnue).

Levers applied (all in nn_trainer, core_engine untouched - golden_eval_unchanged still GREEN):
1. Mild shrink (free config): ACCUM_WIDTH 256→128 (sparse.rs); MlpConfig hidden_sizes
   [256,64,32]→[128,32,32] (model.rs). L1 (the 87%-dominant layer) 256×64→128×32 = 4× fewer
   mul-adds. Sweep ratio 15.45× → 6.20×.
2. Output-major weight layout + wide-crate i16 SIMD dot product on the quantized tail
   (quantized.rs): QLinear stores weights output-major, pre-widened i16, row-padded to 8 lanes;
   quantize_linear transposes burn's input-major weights once; forward runs i16x8.mul_widen →
   i32x8 accumulate → reduce_add. forward_int builds i16 padded activation buffers. wide = "1.5"
   added (stable, portable SSE2/AVX2 + NEON; native-only crate, no WASM concern).
   (An attempt to also SIMD the accumulator refresh column-adds was REVERTED - hand-rolled
   i32x8 gather/scatter measured SLOWER than the autovectorized scalar loop; left scalar with a
   comment. Lesson logged.)

MEASURED (release; hand-crafted eval ~990 ns via inference_cost_refresh_vs_incremental):
- NNUE INCREMENTAL (the plan §4.6 "in-search integer inference" path): 14.7× → **3.8–4.3× hand**
  → **PASSES the ≤~5× gate.**
- NNUE refresh-per-call (Phase-0 conservative bound; what NnueEvaluator uses today): 22.6× → ~8.5×
  microbench, **5.83× on the depth6 sweep**.
- Correctness sacred gates GREEN throughout: quantized_matches_f32_within_tol (mean|Δ|<5.0),
  incremental_accumulator_matches_refresh_over_playout (bit-identity), NNUE search determinism (3-run).

VERDICT: **GO for Phase 1.** The gate is on in-search incremental inference (3.8–4.3×), which is
how the net will really run. Decision (Elias, ns-50): accept current speed; do NOT pull the
Phase-1 accumulator-stack wiring forward just to make the throwaway refresh-per-call path fast.

FIRST PHASE-1 TASK (prerequisite, was always Phase-1 per nnue_evaluator.rs:6–9): wire a
search-owned accumulator stack into find_best_with_evaluator (make+apply / unmake+restore, or
revert) so the search uses the incremental path in-node instead of refresh-per-call. Then the
sweep itself measures <5× end-to-end. Geometry (ACCUM_WIDTH + hidden_sizes) stays a config knob:
Phase 1 may grow it back if gauntlet strength stalls - SIMD headroom can absorb a partial re-widen
under 5×. Passing the SPEED gate is NOT a claim the 128/32 net is strong enough to beat the
heuristic; that is the Phase-1 gauntlet question.

## Update - ns-50 (2026-07-12): FIRST PHASE-1 TASK DONE - incremental accumulator wired into the search

The Phase-1 prerequisite (search-owned accumulator stack; was scoped to Phase 1 per nnue_evaluator.rs:4-9) is implemented on main. The search now maintains ONE incrementally-updated accumulator threaded through make/unmake, read at every leaf via the incremental path - no longer refresh-per-call.

DESIGN (the layering crux): core_engine owns the search + Evaluator trait; nn_trainer (depends on core_engine) owns Accumulator, so the search cannot name it. Solution: an opaque AccHandle newtype (Option<Box<dyn Any + Send>>) + five default-no-op Evaluator methods (uses_accumulator / fresh_acc / clone_acc / push_acc / eval_acc). Object-safe (no Self-typed params; only core_engine types + AccHandle), so every &dyn Evaluator site is untouched. HeuristicEvaluator pays ZERO - empty stack, one bool per node, default methods inert. NnueEvaluator overrides the five to build/clone/apply/forward the real Accumulator via downcast (no-unwrap fallback to the refresh scratch path). Save/restore (clone) update strategy - the golden-test-blessed path (Elias, ns-50); revert stays available as a Phase-2 opt behind the same seam. One clone_acc+push_acc after each make covers all <=3 PVS/LMR re-searches; restore precedes every abort check so parents never read a stale acc.

FILES: core_engine/src/search/evaluator/mod.rs (AccHandle + trait methods); alpha_beta.rs (SearchCtx.acc_stack, root init, null + main make/unmake save-restore, leaf read); quiescence.rs (stand-pat read + loud-move save-restore); nn_trainer/src/nnue_evaluator.rs (5 overrides + gate test). accumulator.rs UNCHANGED (refresh/apply/Clone reused as-is).

GATE (blocking) - GREEN: search_incremental_matches_refresh_per_call asserts the seam-on search returns BIT-IDENTICAL SearchResult {best, score, nodes} to a refresh-forced wrapper (uses_accumulator()==false) across start + seeded walk + corpus FENs x depths {2,4,6}, plus determinism (seam-on twice identical). nodes-equality proves ordering/TT/pruning untouched. core_engine golden_eval_unchanged + unmake_perfectly_restores* + accumulator/quantized suites all GREEN.

SPEED (release, depth6 geo-NPS sweep, game/bench/corpus/corpus.txt): incremental NNUE ~2-3.5x the heuristic (heuristic geo-NPS varies with machine load ~610k-990k; NNUE stable ~283-291k). DOWN from 5.83x refresh-per-call. PASSES the <=5x gate END-TO-END - the search sweep itself now uses the incremental path. (Lower than the isolated microbench 3.8-4.3x because the search shares accumulator state across the tree rather than clone+apply against a fixed undo each call.)

NEXT PHASE-1 TASKS (not started this pass, per scope decision 'wire+verify+measure then stop'): (1) collapse gauntlet.rs three-bracket machinery to a single 100ms track (plan §5.1); (2) unify loadout generators on the corpus builder realistic generator (plan §5.3); (3) mutation self-play loop seeded from the Phase-0 net (plan §4 Phase 1). title: Match-UI quality-of-life pass (P6 grab-bag - not current focus)
body:
A batch of good-to-have match/MP UX requests from P6 (Dorian). Designer call: NOT current focus (a bug fix outranks these), but worth doing together as a UI-review pass. Fold into the same effort as the UI-unification work (ns for help/tutorial) where they share components.

Items:
1. **Move history viewer** - look through old moves in the match screen (relates to ns-18 undo/redo ring buffer; the same action log can back both).
2. **Resign / give-up** - there is currently no way to concede a match. (P6: players wanted a give-up button, never a draw - see oq-58. This is the feature that button request implies.)
3. **On-hover for the in-between step** in move-attacks when click-moving - show the intermediate square/landing preview on hover.
4. **Auto-end turn for humans** when only one legal move remains (skip the trivial confirm).
5. **Time-based competitive MP mode** - a chess-clock mode; clock also ticks during draft, or a separate draft clock. (Cool, explicitly not in focus.)
6. **In-game chat for online play** - "would make online much funnier." (Cool, explicitly not in focus.)
7. **Commit sandbox actions for real** (Dorian) - a way to play out the moves explored in sandbox as actual moves, gated by a check that they were the player's OWN actions. Ties to game-length: sandbox inflates wall-clock (a wanted feature per oq-66, but committing explored lines would recover the time).

Source: P6 Dorian notes (session-42).
